title: First night in Bala, Ontario, and his feature spots
summary: With no rehearsal, Joe played How Long Blues; Louis told him he was an All-Star and the next day asked for Yellow Dog Blues.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x:
Tell me about when you first joined the band.
Did Louis talk to you about how you were going to play?

Of course at that time I knew Louis pretty
well. Because I did a commercial with Louis that Barney
didn't want to do a while back. And we had become pretty
good friends just from socializing with each other. Like I
said, every time he came to Los Angeles or someplace around,
I was with him -- you know, I'd go talk to him. So when I
got in the band, Louis says... We were having just a rundown
on the stuff, and he says, "You've heard the program,
'Blueberry Hill' and whatever," and he says... We didn't
have a rehearsal at all opening night in Ontario, in
Bala(?). And as a solo... As my solo I remember I did the "How Long Blues." That was another tune I used to feature in the low register.
In other words, when you say a solo...

A featured spot. Louis said... First thing he says, "You're an All-Star, now, homeboy; you're an All-Star, so you just get up there and shine" -- I'll never forget those words. He said, "You get up there and you take your 'How Long Blues' and..." And I used to use the "Rose Room" sometimes, like Barney...
How come you didn't use "Yellow Dog Blues"?

Well, I did. But not at first. We wanted to talk that over first, you see. So I had the choice... Once in a while I'd do "Sweet Georgia Brown." Then the next day, that's when Louis says, "Do your 'Yellow Dog Blues.'"
So he let you pick really what you wanted to do on your feature spots.
Well, Louis knew about "Yellow Dog Blues," and he knew that people would like it. He liked it himself.
